validity.researcher_notes: psuwatch.com (22 Jun 2023, on GAIL winning the bid) already gives '175-km long pipeline is to carry environment-friendly fuel to Jammu... initial capacity to carry at least two million standard cubic meters per day' -- matching the sheet's Capacity=2.00 MMSCMD too. dailyexcelsior.com and kashmirlife.net (both Dec 2024, construction-start coverage) repeat 175 km. validity.recommendation: Do NOT add Pakistan to CountriesOrAreas/StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea. Gurdaspur (Punjab) and Jammu (J&K) are both firmly inside India; GAIL is a purely domestic PSU building this line under an Indian PNGRB common-carrier authorisation (Sr. No. 5, GAIL, 160 km, 12.07.2023, under construction), and no Indian or wire source reports any cross-border segment -- a pipeline physically entering Pakistan near a heavily militarised international border in this sector would be major news, not an unremarked construction detail. With RouteAccuracy='very low (straight line/schematic)', the 31.4 km Pakistan landfall reads as a straight-line-geodesic artifact: an unconstrained straight line from Gurdaspur to Jammu can clip the India-Pakistan border zone (which runs close to a direct line through this stretch of Punjab/J&K) even though no real pipeline would ever be routed that way. Flag the geometry for redraw along the real India-only alignment; the CountriesOrAreas fields are correct as-is. This tracks the exact caution the protocol raises for this row.
validity.researcher_notes: No single source directly confirms 'this specific route never crosses Pakistan' (a negative claim), so this is a geographic/logical judgement rather than a citable fact: Gurdaspur district's western edge sits close to the international border, Jammu is well inside India to the northeast, and every source found on this project (PNGRB bid documents, GAIL/press coverage) describes it as a domestic Punjab-to-J&K gas supply line with no international dimension. Combined with RouteAccuracy='very low', the artifact explanation is much more plausible than an actual transnational segment.
